shouldFixDetail.title: summary.specifiedNotLeftover files OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX under a standing its own obligation row denies.
shouldFixDetail.subjectPattern: The subject's summary is a partition of the eleven obligations into five buckets. Three bucket names are exact string equals of a rideStanding value carried by their members: recordedCandidateNotApplied holds the single "recorded-candidate-not-applied" row; honesty holds the single "honesty" row; specifiedNotLeftover holds rows whose rideStanding is the literal "specified-not-leftover". deferredOrRidesElsewhere holds "deferred-to-DR-006" and "rides-G26". In the accepted sarif leftover-join.v7 the fifth bucket, leftoverDesign, held exactly the two rows whose rideStanding is "not-capable-of-riding as execution-only remainder", so the partition was total and every bucket was keyed on a single declared standing. At sarif leftover-join.v10, OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX carries leftoverDesign false, so it no longer qualifies for the leftoverDesign bucket, but it retains rideStanding "not-capable-of-riding as execution-only remainder" and executionObligationOwnerToday "none". It has been placed in specifiedNotLeftover alongside OBL-PREVIEW-NOT-ADVERTISED, OBL-G17, OBL-FC-APPLIC, OBL-FC-OUTFAIL and OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM, all five of which carry rideStanding exactly "specified-not-leftover", and four of which carry executionObligationOwnerToday "Output/operability + CLI/product owners".
shouldFixDetail.refutation: The obvious defence — that specifiedNotLeftover is merely shorthand for every row that is not leftover-design — was tested and fails against the subject's own bytes. Four other rows carry leftoverDesign false and are deliberately kept out of that bucket: OBL-CONTRACT-V15 in recordedCandidateNotApplied, OBL-ADVISORY-HONESTY in honesty, OBL-INACTIVE-DR006 and OBL-G26 in deferredOrRidesElsewhere. The bucket is therefore a standing classification, not a negation of leftoverDesign, and the standing it asserts for OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX is one that obligations[5] itself does not assign. The second defence — that the row's substance now matches OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM, whose remainder is likewise executable fixture bytes — also fails on the subject's own fields: OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM names Output/operability + CLI/product owners as today's execution obligation owner, and OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX names none. The third defence — inheritance, since the placement first appears at sarif leftover-join.v8 and survived two dual-review rounds — is argument from silence, not verification. sarif leftover-join.v8 drew three MUST-FIX from each reviewer and sarif leftover-join.v9 one SHOULD-FIX from each; none of those four rounds of findings reached the summary partition, and the sarif leftover-join.v7 bytes show the partition was consistent before the D-344 remasurement broke it. The defect is real and is the direct residue of flipping obligations[5].leftoverDesign from true to false without touching the field the buckets are keyed on.
shouldFixDetail.whyItMatters: summary is the roll-up a later D-000 recording and the register lift out of this artifact; it exists so a reader need not reconstruct eleven obligation rows. Lifted out, summary.specifiedNotLeftover asserts that OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX is specified and rides an existing owner. The row it summarises asserts the opposite on both counts: no owner today, and not capable of riding, an execution-only remainder. A recorder pinning sarif leftover-join.v10 would carry forward a ride standing and an implied owner for the FC-NONAUTH-TERM fixture remainder that the artifact's own obligation denies. The same lineage has already treated smaller precision defects as findings: sarif leftover-join.v9 was rejected by both reviewers over eight prose tokens missing a lineage stem, which misidentifies nothing a reader could not infer. This misstates a standing outright.
shouldFixDetail.notAMustFix: It does not overstate closure anywhere it counts. summary.leftoverDesign is correctly [OBL-FC-OUTFAIL-FX] and obligations[7].leftoverDesign is correctly true. leftoverDesignOpenStanding, doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone and authorityClaim all state leftover-design of OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX is stale as an authoring claim and leftover-design of OBL-FC-OUTFAIL-FX remains, which is the correct measurement. Nothing is claimed SATISFIED or closed. The defect is confined to which bucket one row sits in.
shouldFixDetail.howToLand: Either update obligations[5].rideStanding to the standing the summary asserts, or move OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX out of summary.specifiedNotLeftover into a bucket that matches "not-capable-of-riding as execution-only remainder". Do not resolve it by flipping obligations[5].leftoverDesign back to true; that measurement is correct and is the warranted act of this cycle.

verdictStatement: REJECT. Zero MUST-FIX, one SHOULD-FIX. The candidate's measurement work is sound and byte-verified: every cited digest matches live bytes, every decision commit resolves, required-now 28 and the DR-122 and DR-107 tokens match live file 08, the eight D-344 copies exist and hash as claimed, and the remasurement of leftover-design of OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX to stale is the exact act D-344 reserved for a leftover-join successor. All four sarif leftover-join.v8 findings and the single sarif leftover-join.v9 finding are landed, exactly and by recount. SF-1 is the residue of that remasurement: flipping obligations[5].leftoverDesign to false moved OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX out of the leftoverDesign bucket and into specifiedNotLeftover without updating the rideStanding the buckets are keyed on, so the roll-up now asserts a standing and an implied riding owner that the obligation row itself denies. Under ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, the verdict is REJECT.
